title: Delhi HC Disposes IFF and SFLC Pleas After X Corp Says Fake Delhi Police Notices Blocked Their Accounts
case_name: Internet Freedom Foundation & Anr. v. Union of India & Ors., with a connected petition by the Software Freedom Law Centre
citation: Order dated 6 November 2026 (Justice Amit Mahajan); case number not independently confirmed in this run
card_summary: X accounts of the Internet Freedom Foundation and the Software Freedom Law Centre were blocked by takedown notices purporting to be from the Delhi Police. X Corp told the Delhi High Court its check found the notices came from an impostor, not the police, and that it had filed its own complaint to trace the sender. Justice Amit Mahajan disposed of both petitions on 6 November 2026 on that statement.
card_tip: A platform served a takedown notice that cites police authority should verify the sender through official channels before acting, since complying with a forged notice can itself draw court scrutiny.
verification_notes: The blocking of the IFF and SFLC accounts, X's statement that the notices were sent by an impostor and not the Delhi Police, X's own police complaint to trace the sender, the 6 November 2026 disposal before Justice Amit Mahajan, and the liberty granted to the petitioners to return are consistent across the Bar and Bench, LiveLaw and Internet Freedom Foundation reports seen in this run (the last being the petitioner's own account of the hearing). No source in this run gave a W.P.(C) number for either petition, so the citation field records only the date and bench; this should be confirmed against the Delhi High Court's order before any further use. The order does not decide who sent the fake notices; that remains the subject of a separate police complaint.
